assumptions: Selected clinics have enough valuable cancellations that refill gains cover fees.
Clinic-managed messaging and minimum necessary data can support a lawful initial pilot.
Recovered attendance can be attributed with an agreed counterfactual method.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A controlled paid pilot in a high-value specialty demonstrating incremental filled slots, positive clinic ROI, low opt-out rates, and a credible integration path.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Charging against verified recovered visits aligns price with a measurable utilization gain and goes beyond undifferentiated reminder messaging.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Unused clinical capacity is economically real, but Polish specialty-level loss, incremental refill rates, and willingness to share recovered revenue are unknown.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Recurring fees plus performance revenue can align incentives and support good margins, though integration CAC, attribution disputes, and compliance overhead may erode economics.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish private outpatient clinics are accessible and numerous, but the beachhead needs tighter specialty selection based on slot value and cancellation frequency.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Vendor-neutral refill attribution could support a niche position, but scheduling vendors can readily add waitlist matching and control core integrations.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: The rail could expand into scheduling optimization, deposits, demand forecasting, patient recall, and broader capacity marketplaces.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Specialty response models and workflow data could improve over time, but clinics own patient relationships and incumbents control integration access.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: One-tap cancellation, immediate waitlist refill, and outcome pricing could materially outperform reminders, but incremental causality has not been demonstrated.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Messaging automation and AI scoring make implementation cheaper, but there is no singular regulatory or market catalyst.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Practice-management and medical-accounting partners could provide repeatability, but there is no integration or referral commitment and partners may demand substantial economics.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A clinic-managed CSV pilot is feasible, while special-category data, lawful messaging, causality measurement, integrations, and trust require disciplined specialist support.

highest_value_structural_change: Narrow the initial product to one high-value specialty and secure a practice-management integration that enables automatic cancellation, matching, and attendance attribution.
main_structural_strength: Outcome pricing connects the product directly to recovered clinic revenue and creates a clear ROI narrative.
primary_score_limiter: The incremental effect beyond existing reminders is unproven, while incumbent schedulers control the most scalable distribution and integration points.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Existing practice software already sends reminders and can add refill features, while automated health-data workflows create compliance and trust burdens.
